Lean line 45: `∀ s t h, overStrand ⟨{s,t},_⟩ = s` with s.1 = i; since overStrand x ∈ {s,t} and s.1 = i ≠ j = t.1, `overStrand x = s ⟺ (overStrand x).1 = i`, i.e. "component i is over at every mixed crossing"; line 46 is the same for j. If one insisted the printed hypothesis were the block-wide one of mp:stack, Lean's per-pair hypothesis is weaker, making the Lean theorem stronger, never weaker. Vacuous case (no mixed crossings) agrees on both sides (sum 0).

(3) Integrality: `∃ k : ℤ, mixedSignSum D i j = 2 * k` (line 42) with `mixedSignSum : ℤ` is exactly "half-sum ∈ ℤ"; k may be negative. The summation set is the same MixedPair i j set as clause (b), matching the proof (1571-1573 "differs from the zero fixed-order sum by twice an integer").

Counting check underlying all three: `Adjacent s t` (LinkDiagram.lean:142-143) requires s.1 = t.1, so for i ≠ j cross-component pairs are never adjacent and `MixedPair i j s t ⟺ s.1 = i ∧ t.1 = j ∧ (seg s ∩ seg t).Nonempty` (IsCrossing, 246-247). Each unordered mixed crossing {s,t} gives exactly one ordered pair with first entry on i (the swap fails t.1 = i), so no double counting. `tail_off` (cross-component pairs are never IncidentTail, so no vertex of one component lies on any edge of the other) plus `transverse` make each such meeting a single interior transverse point; `no_triple` makes distinct pairs have distinct points (`crossingPoint_injective` 463-480). Hence Lean crossings biject with the printed transverse intersections, and `det (dir s) (dir t)` with s on i is det(u₁,u₂) in the printed component order. i ≠ j : Fin D.Γ.c renders "two distinct components"; c ≥ 1 built in renders "actual".

No configuration separates the Lean fields from the printed lemma.
